He played college basketball for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. Born in [[Mississauga]], [[Ontario]], he played high school basketball at [[Father Michael Goetz Secondary School|Father Michael Goetz]] in his hometown. In 2012, he started playing [[college basketball]] for [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]]. He later played a total of 20 regular-season [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) games with the [[Utah Jazz]] and the [[Indiana Pacers]]. ==High school career== One of the top prospects out of Canada, Long was ranked as the 7th-best player in Canada according to North Pole Hoops. He participated in the 2011 All-Canada Classic, a showcase of the best Canadian basketball players and played for the CIA Bounce AAU program, the top AAU summer circuit in Canada. He played with NBA players [[Tristan Thompson]] and [[Cory Joseph]], and future [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclone]] teammate [[Melvin Ejim]] while competing for REDA Red in the National Prep School Athletic Association in 2011–12. Naz played for Findlay Prep in Las Vegas, Nev., during the 2010–11 season, helping the Prep Pilots to a 28–4 record and their third-straight [[ESPN]] Rise National High School Invitational appearance where he was teammates with [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas']] [[Myck Kabongo]]. He prepped at [[Montrose Christian School|Montrose Christian]] [[Rockville, Maryland|(Rockville, Md)]] in 2009–10, teaming with [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke's]] Josh Hairston During his recruitment he received offers from [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]], [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]], [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]], eventually committing to the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Naz saw action in 18 games as a freshman, averaging 1.4 points and 1.0 assists. He tallied seven points vs. [[Southern Jaguars basketball|Southern]] and handed out seven assists vs. [[Alabama A&M Bulldogs basketball|Alabama A&M]]. ===Sophomore season=== Long played in all 36 games, making seven starts and establishing himself as a clutch 3-point threat. He averaged 7.1 points per game and shot 40 percent from behind the arc, finishing fourth in the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] in 3-point field goal percentage (40.0) and seventh in 3-pointers made (1.8). His 64 3-pointers ranks as the 17th-most by a [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclone]] in a single season. He made at least four 3-pointers in seven games. He hit a 30-foot three at the buzzer to send the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclones]] to overtime against [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]]{{cite web|url=http://thebiglead.com/2014/03/08/naz-long-hit-a-deep-3-pointer-to-send-iowa-stateoklahoma-state-to-overtime/ |title=Naz Long Hit a Deep 3-Pointer to Send Iowa State/Oklahoma State to Overtime |publisher=The Big Lead |date= March 8, 2014|access-date=2016-03-29}} and in ISU's game at [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] earlier in the season, Long drilled a three to send the game to triple-OT.{{cite web|last=Eisenberg |first=Jeff |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/naz-long-game-saving-three-helps-iowa-state-053303860--ncaab.html |title=Naz Long's game-saving three helps Iowa State end its Stillwater hex | The Dagger - Yahoo Sports |website=Sports.yahoo.com |date=2014-02-04 |access-date=2016-03-29}} He earned Phillips 66 [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Player of the Week honors after hitting 8-of-11 3-pointers in the Cyclones' season-opening win against [[UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington]] and finishing with a career-high 26 points in the game.{{cite web|last=Dauster |first=Rob |url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/11/10/deandre-kane-naz-long-impress-in-iowa-states-win-over-unc-wilmington/ |title=DeAndre Kane, Naz Long impress in Iowa State's win over UNC Wilmington – CollegeBasketballTalk |website=Collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com |date=2013-11-10 |access-date=2016-03-29}} He went 4-of-6 from long range to score 16 points in the Cyclones' win against No. 7 [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]]. Long played a key role in ISU's Big 12 Tournament run, making 7-of-10 threes and averaging 10 points and going 4-of-6 from behind the arc in the championship game against Baylor. In the third round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], Long hit three 3-pointers in the final 5:10, including one that tied the game at 81, as ISU rallied to defeat [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite web|url=http://thegazette.com/2014/03/23/naz-long-keeps-hitting-big-shots-for-iowa-state |title=> Naz Long keeps hitting big shots for Iowa State |publisher=The Gazette |date=2014-04-01 |access-date=2016-03-29}} He averaged 7.1 points per game and shot 40 percent from behind the arc, finishing fourth in the Big 12 in 3-point field goal percentage (40.0) and seventh in 3-pointers made (1.8). His 64 3-pointers ranks as the 17th-most by a Cyclone in a single season. ===Junior season=== Long saw action in all 34 games, making 33 starts and hit four or more threes in a game six times. He scored a team-high 20 points in Iowa State's regular season win against Kansas and connected on 5-of-9 threes to lead Iowa State with 21 points in win at [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{cite web|author=Chad Leistikow |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/12/12/naz-long-helps-no-14-iowa-state-beat-iowa-90-75/20337987/ |title=Naz Long, Iowa State dismantle Iowa in Cy-Hawk showdown |website=Usatoday.com |date=2014-12-12 |access-date=2016-03-29}} He drilled 7-of-10 threes and scored a season-high 24 points against [[Mississippi Valley State Delta Devils basketball|Mississippi Valley State]].{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2014/12/31/naz-long-iowa-state-men-mississippi-valley-state-birch/21136579/ |title=Naz Long's strong 3-point shooting night makes life easy |website=Desmoinesregister.com |date=2014-12-31 |access-date=2016-03-29}} Naz grabbed a career-high seven boards in win against [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. He averaged 10.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.0 assists. He hit a team-high 77 three-pointers, the eighth most in a single season by a Cyclone. He was second in the Big 12 averaging 2.3 three-pointers made per game and finished the season tied for fifth in the league shooting 39.1 percent behind the arc. Naz had ISU's third-longest streak of games with a three-pointer come to an end at 21 games. He shot 44.9 percent from the field despite 77.5 percent of his shots coming from three-point range and is tied for fifth all-time at Iowa State with 146 three-pointers made. Long suffered a labral tears in both of his hips during the season. In the offseason he had separate surgeries to repair each tear.{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2015/05/07/iowa-state--basketball-star-naz-long-undergoes-hip-surgery/70941766/ |title=Cyclone Naz Long's second hip surgery went well; rehab starts Monday |website=Desmoinesregister.com |date=2015-05-07 |access-date=2016-03-29}} ===Senior season=== [[File:Naz Mitrou-Long-2.jpg|thumb|right|alt=Naz Mitrou-Long sitting on the bench, during Iowas State's 79–76 to Oklahoma.|Mitrou-Long had to sit out for most of the [[2015–16 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|2015–16 season]].]] Naz played in the first eight games this season for the fifth-ranked Cyclones, averaging 12.0 points in 31.6 minutes. He got a rest against [[Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball|Arkansas–Pine Bluff]], with coach [[Steve Prohm]] commenting that his situation would be re-evaluated every week.{{cite news |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/2015/12/13/iowa-state-star-miss-sundays-game/77249368/ |title=Naz Mitrou-Long rests up against Arkansas-Pine Bluff |last=Birch |first=Tommy |newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=December 13, 2015}} On 15 December 2015, he decided to sit out the rest of the season due to persistent pain from his hip surgeries.{{cite news |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2015/12/15/naz-mitrou-long-iowa-state-cyclones-out-for-season/77380322/ |title=Iowa State's Naz Mitrou-Long to miss rest of season |last=Birch |first=Tommy |newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=December 15, 2015}} Mitrou-Long commented on his decision: "I feel the need to take time off to allow myself to rehab with our training staff to get back to where I can perform at my peak level on the basketball court".{{cite news |url=http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/college/mens-basketball/iowa-states-naz-mitrou-long-out-for-the-season-20151215 |title=Iowa State's Naz Mitrou-Long out for the season |last=Montz |first=Dylan |newspaper=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |location=[[Cedar Rapids]] |date=December 15, 2015}} Iowa State coach Prohm supported Mitrou-Long's decision to sit out to rehabilitate, while adding his belief that the team could react in a positive manner. Naz was awarded a [[Redshirt (college sports)|medical redshirt]] by the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]], thus becoming eligible for the 2016–2017 season.{{cite news |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2016/04/29/naz-mitrou-long-returns-to-iowa-state-steve-prohm/83714704/ |title=It's official: Naz Mitrou-Long is back for Iowa State |last=Peterson |first=Randy |newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=April 29, 2016}} ===Redshirt senior season=== Going into his redshirt senior season, Long was named in the It was a little weird, but man it was a good time"''.{{cite news |url=http://www.iowastatedaily.com/sports/article_a373198a-aae4-11e6-b1f0-6f7d0d367ee9.html |title=Naz Mitrou-Long, Cyclones best Mount St. Mary's 73-55 in 'Long family reunion |last=Young |first=Ryan |newspaper=[[Iowa State Daily]] |date=November 14, 2016 |archive-date=January 9, 2017 |access-date=January 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170109021821/http://www.iowastatedaily.com/sports/article_a373198a-aae4-11e6-b1f0-6f7d0d367ee9.html |url-status=dead }} Against the [[2016–17 Drake Bulldogs men's basketball team|Drake Bulldogs]], Mitrou-Long set a new career-high in scoring with 37 points on 8 of 12 three-pointers.{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyprogress.com/mitrou-long-s-points-help-iowa-state-beat-drake/article_0f070313-59fa-58ee-a5e1-4e49871c6caa.html |title=Mitrou-Long's 37 points help Iowa State beat Drake 97-80 |last=Meredith |first=Luke |newspaper=[[The Daily Progress]] |date=December 17, 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} At the end of his redshirted senior season, Mitrou-Long would be named for the official All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Second Team for the work he put in that year for Iowa State. ==Professional career== ===Salt Lake City Stars (2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]], Mitrou-Long played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2017 NBA Summer League]]. He later signed with the Utah Jazz for their training camp squad. After getting cut from the team, he was assigned to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] in the [[NBA G League]]. ===Utah Jazz (2017–2019)=== After showing promising results for his playing in [[Salt Lake City Stars]], on December 22, 2017, Mitrou-Long signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]], taking the spot that was originally held by [[Nate Wolters]].{{Cite news|last=Bolerjack|first=Nick|date=December 23, 2017|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-naz-mitrou-long-two-way-contract|title=Jazz Sign Naz Mitrou-Long to Two-way Contract {{!}} Utah Jazz|work=Utah Jazz|access-date=December 23, 2017}} This move saw him split playing time between the Jazz and the Stars for the rest of the length of his contract. Mitrou-Long made his NBA debut four days later, recording a three-pointer in a blowout 107–83 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. However, on January 13, 2018, Mitrou-Long was waived from the Jazz in order to sign former college teammate [[Georges Niang]].{{Cite web|last=Woodyard|first=Eric|date=14 January 2018|title=Utah Jazz sign Georges Niang to two-way deal after waiving college teammate|url=https://www.deseret.com/2018/1/14/20625151/utah-jazz-sign-georges-niang-to-two-way-deal-after-waiving-college-teammate|access-date=17 October 2020|website=Deseret News|language=en}} He was re-signed by the Jazz on February 11, 2018, to a 10-day contract.{{cite news|title=Jazz Sign Naz Mitrou-Long to 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-naz-mitrou-long-10-day-contract|access-date=12 February 2018|work=Utah Jazz|date=11 February 2018}} After his first 10-day contract expired on February 21, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Jazz three days later.{{cite news|title=Jazz Sign Naz Mitrou-Long to Second 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-naz-mitrou-long-second-10-day-contract|access-date=24 February 2018|work=Utah Jazz|date=24 February 2018}} ===Salt Lake City Stars (2018–2019)=== On January 16, 2018, Mitrou-Long was reacquired by the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{Cite news|last=Rueckert|first=Daniel|url=http://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/news/stars-reacquire-naz-mitrou-long/|title=Stars Reacquire Naz Mitrou-Long|work=NBA.com|date=January 16, 2018|access-date=January 18, 2018|archive-date=April 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420033734/https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/news/stars-reacquire-naz-mitrou-long/|url-status=dead}} He returned to Salt Lake City once again on February 21, 2018, after his 10-day contract expired. Mitrou-Long left Salt Lake City once again for his second 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]], and returned to Salt Lake City after the second 10-day contract expired. He averaged 18.0 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 4.6 assists per game with Salt Lake City.{{cite news|title=Final 2017-18 NBA G League stats for ex-Iowa collegians|url=http://www.thegazette.com/final-nba-g-league-stats-for-ex-iowa-collegians-20180327|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=March 27, 2018}} In July 2019, Mitrou-Long joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the 2019 [[NBA Summer League]]. ===Indiana Pacers (2019–2020)=== On July 31, 2019, Mitrou-Long signed a two-way contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Justin Holiday; Sign Naz Mitrou-Long to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-justin-holiday-sign-naz-mitrou-long-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 31, 2019|date=July 31, 2019}} On November 18, 2019, Mitrou-Long scored a career-high 12 points while getting three rebounds, three assists and one steal in a 115–86 win against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Mitrou-Long Ready for Opportunity, Wherever it Comes|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/mitrou-long-ready-opportunity-wherever-it-comes|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 2, 2020|date=November 22, 2019}} In the G League, he averaged 13.7 points, 6.1 assists and 5.9 rebounds per game. On December 19, Mitrou-Long was waived by the Pacers.On{{cite web |last1=Anidos |first1=Roberto |title=Mitrou-Long y Mantzaris, opciones para el puesto de base del Panathinaikos |url=https://piratasdelbasket.net/mitrou-long-y-mantzaris-opciones-para-el-puesto-de-base-del-panathinaikos/ |website=Piratas del Basket |access-date=July 16, 2020 |language=Spanish |date=April 15, 2020}} ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2021)=== On January 11, 2021, Mitrou-Long signed with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA G League]] as an affiliate player.{{Cite web|url=https://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/fort-wayne-mad-ants-announce-2021-roster-for-single-site-season|title=Fort Wayne Mad Ants' announce 2021 roster for single site season|date=January 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 29, 2021}} He averaged 13.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.1 steals per game. ===Basket Brescia Leonessa (2021–2022)=== On July 30, 2021, Mitrou-Long signed with [[Basket Brescia Leonessa]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Nazareth Mitrou-Long is a newcomer at Brescia rebounds and 5 assists per game, leading the team to the 3rd place in the domestic league regular season standings. ===Olimpia Milano (2022–2023)=== On June 27, 2022, Mitrou-Long signed a two-year contract with Italian champions [[Olimpia Milano]].{{cite web|title=Milan signs shooting guard Mitrou-Long|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/milan-signs-shooting-guard-mitrou-long/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|date=June 27, 2023|access-date=June 28, 2023}} On June 27, 2023, he parted ways with the club. ===Žalgiris Kaunas (2023)=== On June 27, 2023, Mitrou-Long signed a two-year (1+1) deal with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Mitrou-Long to replace Isaiah Taylor in Zalgiris|url=https://zalgiris.lt/en/news/bc-zalgiris/122296/|publisher=[[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Mitrou-Long|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/zalgiris-signs-naz-mitrou-long/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|date=June 27, 2023|access-date=June 27, 2023}} On November 21, 2023, Žalgiris announced that the club is parting ways with Mitrou-Long by mutual decision.{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-197719-naz-mitrou-long-officially-leaves-zalgiris-joins-olympiacos.html|title=Naz Mitrou-Long officially leaves Zalgiris, joins Olympiacos|date=November 21, 2023|website=BasketNews}} He averaged 4.1 points, 1.2 rebounds, 1.0 assist, and 1.8 PIR per game in 9 EuroLeague appearances for Žalgiris.{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/players/22180-naz-mitrou-long/statistics/leagues/25-euroleague/2023.html|title=Naz Mitrou-Long stats in Zalgiris|date=November 21, 2023|website=BasketNews}} ===Olympiacos Piraeus (2023–2025)=== On November 21, 2023, Mitrou-Long signed a three-year contract with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]] in anticipation of the acquisition of his Greek passport and citizenship. On December 21 of the same year, Mitrou-Long received his passport and was registered as a domestic player. On July 10, 2025, Mitrou-Long was waived by the Greek club. ===Napoli Basket (2025–2026)=== On September 9th of 2025, Mitrou-Long signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli Basket]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{Cite web|title=Napoli announced the signing of Naz Mitrou-Long on a one-year deal|url=https://basketballsphere.com/en/napoli-announced-the-signing-of-naz-mitrou-long-on-a-one-year-deal/|access-date=November 22, 2025|website=basketballsphere.com|language=en}} ===PAOK Thessaloniki (2026-)=== On June 5th of 2026, Mitrou-Long returned again to Greece, after his tenure at [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], signing a three year contract with [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL).{{Cite web |date=2026-06-05 |title=Επίσημα στον ΠΑΟΚ ο Ναζ Μήτρου-Λονγκ για τα επόμενα τρία χρόνια |url=https://www.sdna.gr/mpasket/1436798_episima-ston-paok-o-naz-mitroy-longk-gia-ta-epomena-tria-hronia |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=SDNA |language=el}} ==National team career== Mitrou-Long is a member of the senior men's [[Greek men's national basketball team|Greek national team]]. On 13 February 2024, he was called on to represent Greece at the [[2025 FIBA EuroBasket qualifiers]].[https://sportstherapy.gr/basket/ethniki-ellados-basket/18980/ethniki-andron-oi-kliseis-tou-spanouli-gia-to-parathyro-tou-fevrouariou/ Οι κλήσεις του Σπανούλη για το παράθυρο του Φεβρουαρίου sportstherapy.gr] On 26 February 2024, he was on Greece's 12 man game roster for their against the [[Netherlands men's national basketball team|Netherlands]], but he didn't play in the |url=https://www.iowastatedaily.com/sports/the-power-of-a-name-naz-mitrou-long/article_8cf78802-97f9-11e5-aa86-2b5a47667b5d.html|title=The power of a name: Naz Mitrou-Long |last=Dibie |first=Max |archive-date=December 26, 2020 }} His mother Georgia was born in [[Sparta, Laconia|Sparta]], [[Greece]] and immigrated to Canada along with her family when she was a child.[https://www.sfina.gr/mpasket/paok-a1/mitrou-longk-eipa-ochi-stin-kanada-gia-na-paixo-me-tin-ellada/ Μήτρου Λονγκ Είπα όχι στον Καναδά] His brother, [[Elijah Mitrou-Long]], previously played college basketball for [[Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball|Mount St. Mary's University]] before transferring to the [[University of Texas]] in his junior year.{{cite news |url=http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/college/mens-basketball/iowa-state-set-to-host-mount-st-marys-and-naz-mitrou-longs-brother-elijah-20161113 |title=Iowa State set to host Mount St. Mary's and Naz Mitrou-Long's brother, Elijah |last=Montz |first=Dylan |location = [[Cedar Rapids]] | newspaper=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |date=November 13, 2016}} After one year with the Longhorns, he transferred to the [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]]. In summer 2015, Mitrou-Long decided to display his full last name on his jersey to honor his mother; up to that point his jersey had only his father's name on it.{{cite news |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/2015/07/23/naz-mitrou-long-iowa-state-cyclones/30575727/ |title=Iowa State senior Mitrou-Long honors mom with name change |last=Birch |first=Tommy
